newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. rights chief said to be quitting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. rights chief said to be quitting.

text.p: United Nations human rights chief Jose Ayala Lasso is expected to quit his post soon to become Ecuador's foreign minister, U.N. officials said on Thursday.

Ayala Lasso, a former U.N. ambassador and international lawyer from Ecuador, is expected to return home next week and take up his new post as foreign minister, Ecuador's deputy foreign minister Diego Ribadeneira announced in Quito.

Ayala Lasso, the first U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights since April 1994, was expected to return to Geneva late on Thursday from a trip to Rwanda and Burundi and could not be reached for comment.
The human rights chief is elected by the U.N. General Assembly on the nomination of the Secretary-General. Ayala Lasso's four-year term was up for renewal next year.
Some diplomats and human rights groups have criticised Ayala Lasso for his relatively low profile in drawing public attention to abuses and violence.
In a recent letter to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, Human Rights Watch executive director Kenneth Roth criticised the Ecuadorean's preference for quiet diplomacy.
Ayala Lasso has also been criticised by some Western diplomats for reacting slowly to violence and killings in Burundi and the Balkans.
U.N. sources said he may be replaced by a more aggressive and forceful rights chief. One name mentioned as a possible successor was Irish President Mary Robinson.
